samples.summary: No test covers the newly *created* merge's alias recalculation (dependants of cells that become covered by a pasted merge)
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges`/`clearCellsUnderMerge` add every covered sref of a *pasted* block to `changedSrefs` precisely so formulas that read through the new alias recalculate (sheet.ts comment at the head of `applyPasteMerges`). The suite tests only the opposite direction: 'should recalculate dependants of a merge the paste removed' (merge.test.ts:429). There is no test where e.g. `=B3+1` exists, a merged block is pasted onto A3:B3, and B3 starts aliasing A3 — so a regression that omitted the created-block srefs from `changedSrefs` would ship with a stale displayed formula result and every new test would still pass. Searched merge.test.ts for the whole new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block and grepped the sheets test dir for `paste(`.

samples.summary: Spill branches of the extracted `clearCellsUnderMerge` and the new `unblockedAnchors` recalculation branch in `paste` are untested
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` contains ghost-deletion, `spillBlocked`, and `consumeSpillBlocker` → `unblockedAnchors` logic, and `paste` gained a new `changedSrefs.size > 0 || unblockedAnchors.size > 0` recalculation branch plus the pre-recalc ordering of `applyPasteMerges`. `grep -n 'spill|MUNIT|MMULT'` in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts returns no matches, and the new copy-paste tests use only plain values, so no test writes a spilling formula or a blocked spill under a destination that a pasted merge covers. A defect (orphaned ghosts, or a blocked anchor never re-spilling after the paste clears its blocker) would ship silently.

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` rewritten to use `rangeOf`, but no test asserts the selection/activeCell after a paste
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the hand-rolled bounding-box loop in `selectPastedRange` with `rangeOf(grid)` and changes the single-cell check. Grepping packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts for `activeCell|ranges|selection` returns no matches, and the new merge copy-paste tests assert only merge maps and display strings. Nothing would catch a regression in post-paste selection (including the merge case, where the grid box is smaller than the pasted merged block, so the selected range under-covers it).

samples.summary: `snapshotMergesIn`'s filter (blocks only clipped by the copied range are excluded from the buffer) has no test
samples.evidence: `snapshotMergesIn` filters with `isRangeInRange(m.range, range)`; its own doc comment says the UI cannot reach that case and the filter guards a programmatic caller. No test in the new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block constructs a programmatic partially-clipping copy range (all use selectStart/selectEnd, which normalize). Low impact, but the guard is untested.

samples.evidence: `refusalMessage` gained a `merge-paste-partial` case; grep for `refusalMessage` across packages/sheets shows only src/view/worksheet.ts:98 and :423 — no test file references it. Model-level refusal reasons are tested (merge.test.ts:302, autofill.test.ts:220) but the user-facing string mapping is not, consistent with existing practice.

mergedFrom.summary: New cut test does not assert the clipped source cells / stale data left behind by the moved block

finding.summary: No test that a CUT paste still refuses when it clips a merged block that is NOT part of the cut
finding.evidence: The delta weakens the split-guard for cuts (`planPasteMerges` filters `getMergesIntersecting(destRange)` by a `travelling` set when `isCut`). The only test covering the weakened path is the new one at merge.test.ts:528, which asserts the *non*-refusal direction (its own block). The one refusal test, 'should refuse a paste that would split a destination block' (merge.test.ts:476-502), uses `sheet.copy()`, so it exercises `isCut === false` only. I grepped every `sheet.cut()` call in packages/sheets/test (merge.test.ts:395, 540 and clipboard.test.ts) and none combines a cut with a destination that clips a foreign merged block. Consequence: if the exclusion were over-broad (e.g. skipping the check entirely for cuts, or a wrong anchor comparison), a cut paste would split a destination merge and corrupt the merge map with a green suite.

verdict.reason: The cut-path branch of the paste split-guard (sheet.ts:2428-2440, `travelling` filter gated on `isCut`) has no test covering its refusal direction. Searching independently of the reviewer's greps — `setOnRefusal` repo-wide (only autofill.test.ts:211,227 and merge.test.ts:266,288,309,482,509,532,578), `getMerges|mergeSelection|setMerges` across every test/__tests__/spec file, all `.cut(` call sites repo-wide including packages/frontend, and `merge-paste-partial` repo-wide — the only paste-refusal test is merge.test.ts:476-502, which uses `sheet.copy()` (line 490), i.e. isCut===false. clipboard.test.ts, which holds most `sheet.cut()` calls, contains no occurrence of "merge" at all. The one cut+merge test (merge.test.ts:528-552) cuts A1:C3 so the clipped B2:C2 block is itself travelling, and asserts `refusals` is empty — the non-refusal direction only. Consequently an over-broad exclusion (e.g. skipping the containment check entirely for cuts) would split a foreign destination merged block, corrupting the merge map, with the suite green. That is a data-affecting guard silently weakened with no meaningful test: major under the test-adequacy rubric. No counterexample found.
